details:
TerraShift AI

What does the project do and how does it work?

TerraShift AI is a crop-rotation decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the theme “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data”.

The platform combines NASA climate data with farm information to help users explore crop choices, simulate crop rotations and compare different farming scenarios. Users can enter their farm location, land area, soil properties and irrigation details. The platform retrieves climate information for the selected location through the NASA POWER Daily Point API.

It uses eight NASA POWER parameters: temperature, maximum and minimum temperature, corrected precipitation, relative humidity, root-zone wetness, solar radiation and wind speed. These parameters provide climate context for exploring crop suitability and rotation scenarios.

TerraShift AI has six main modules: Farm Profile and Provenance, Crop Library and Overrides, Climate Explorer and Data Coverage, Rotation Simulator and Weights, Compare and Insights, and Methodology and AI Advisor.

Its scoring model evaluates four dimensions: Soil, Water, Climate and Diversity. The default weights are 30%, 30%, 25% and 15%, respectively. Users can adjust these weights and compare results on a scale of 0 to 100.

What are the benefits?

TerraShift AI brings farm information and NASA climate data together in one platform. It helps users understand local climate conditions, explore different crop-rotation combinations and compare scenarios using consistent evaluation criteria.

Its adjustable weights allow users to explore how different priorities affect the results. The platform also provides climate data coverage information and explains its methodology, helping users understand where the information comes from and how the results are calculated.

The interface supports English, Hindi and Kannada to make the platform more accessible to users in India.

What is the intended impact?

The intended impact is to make climate-informed crop-rotation planning easier to explore and understand. TerraShift AI aims to encourage better-informed agricultural discussions by connecting Earth observation data with farm-level information.

It can serve as an exploratory decision-support tool for farmers, students, researchers and agricultural practitioners. It is designed to support local knowledge and decision-making, not replace farmers or agricultural experts.

The scores are illustrative heuristic outputs. They are not validated soil-health assessments or predictions of crop yield, income or future climate conditions. Local agricultural validation is necessary before using the results for real farm decisions.

What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed as a software-based web platform using:

  • Frontend: React 19 and TanStack Start.
  • Platform and backend: Base44 SDK, entities and server functions.
  • Data source: NASA POWER Daily Point API.
  • Programming language: JavaScript.
  • Scoring and calculations: Deterministic JavaScript-based scoring model.
  • Charts and visualisation: Recharts.
  • AI functionality: TanStack AI through the Base44 AI gateway.
  • Location support: OpenStreetMap Nominatim and manual coordinate input.
  • Languages: English, Hindi and Kannada.

The project does not require dedicated physical hardware. It is designed to be accessed through a web browser.

How is the project creative?

The creative aspect of TerraShift AI is its combination of NASA Earth observation data, farm-level information and an adjustable crop-rotation simulation in one platform.

Instead of presenting climate data only as charts, it connects climate context to crop-rotation scenarios. Users can change evaluation priorities, compare alternative plans and explore how different combinations affect their scores.

The platform also includes data provenance, coverage information and methodology explanations so users can understand the basis of the results rather than receiving an unexplained recommendation.

What factors did the team consider?

The project considered farm location, soil properties, irrigation availability, land area, climate conditions, crop characteristics and crop diversity. It also considered the importance of transparent data sources, missing data handling, adjustable scoring weights and accessibility for users speaking different languages.

Another important factor was the distinction between NASA-provided climate information and farmer-entered or crop-library information. Soil properties are supplied by the user or represented through crop-library assumptions, rather than being treated as direct measurements from NASA POWER.

TerraShift AI was designed as an exploratory tool with clearly communicated limitations. Its results require local agronomic knowledge and field-level validation before they can be used as practical farming recommendations.

NOTE :

Geographical Scope: TerraShift AI is currently designed to support agricultural locations within India. Its location search and coordinate validation are restricted to India. International coverage can be incorporated in future versions by extending geographical validation and integrating region-specific agricultural datasets.

Geographical Limitation: The current implementation does not include a dedicated land-water mask. Therefore, water bodies are not automatically identified or excluded during coordinate selection. The application uses NASA POWER gridded climate data for the selected coordinates, which should be interpreted with this limitation in mind.
